summary: Slovakia applies the EU's Schengen visa rules. Your Europe says EU nationals can travel freely in the EU and in Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland with a valid passport or national identity card. Under Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, nationals of the third countries listed in Annex II are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period, and nationals of those listed in Annex I must hold a visa when crossing the external borders.

The UK government says you could get a heavy fine without a vignette.

The UK government says that if you need help from the Slovak Mountain Rescue Service (HZS) you will have to meet costs of up to 1,000 euros, advises making sure your insurance includes rescue costs, and says anyone ignoring or violating HZS rules or instructions will get a fine of up to 3,320 euros.
The EU says visa-exempt travellers will need an ETIAS travel authorisation for the 30 European countries requiring it, and that ETIAS is currently not in operation.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Slovakia?
faq.answer: Your Europe says EU nationals can travel freely in the EU and in Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland with a valid passport or national identity card. Under Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, nationals of the third countries listed in Annex II, which include the United States, are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period, and nationals of the countries listed in Annex I must hold a visa when crossing the external borders.

faq.question: Is Slovakia in the Schengen Area?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK government says Slovakia follows Schengen area rules, that the Schengen area includes Slovakia, and that visits to Schengen countries in the 180 days before you travel count towards your 90 days.

faq.question: Will I need ETIAS for Slovakia?
faq.answer: The EU says ETIAS is currently not in operation and no applications are collected at this point, and that it will announce the start date several months before launch. It says applying directly through the official ETIAS website will cost EUR 20, that applicants under 18 or over 70 years of age are exempt from the payment, and that an ETIAS will be valid for three years or until your passport expires, whichever comes first.

faq.question: What currency does Slovakia use?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says the currency of Slovakia is the euro (EUR).
